messages.author: ebac19664dad3407
messages.subject: Re: How to plot frequency distributions?
parts:
If you're using rstan and you're just asking about making frequency plots (not specifically about a layout that has frequency on the left and traceplots on the right), then I'd recommend looking at the R package ggmcmc, which generates a lot of nice plots.

You have to convert your stanfit object into a coda object, but rstan has functions for that. The old way (before rstan 2.7) was 
coda_obj <- mcmc.list(lapply(1:ncol(stanfit_obj), function(x) mcmc(as.array(stanfit_obj)[,x,])))

But now you can use

coda_obj <- As.mcmc.list(stanfit_obj)

(Be careful about capitalizing the first "A" in "As.mcmc.list" because there's a coda function "as.mcmc.list" that doesn't know about stanfit objects)

Look at ggs_histogram and ggs_density in particular, and you may find ggs_caterpillar useful as well.
